research_updates.title: Operator chronology, investment and boundary audit
research_updates.notes: Reviewed the 2018 groundbreaking, current location page, 2024 impact study and June 2026 expansion release. Retained separately the $600 million original plan, TVA's approximately $600 million FY2020 capital-program result, the greater-than-$980 million 2024 historical snapshot, current greater-than-$2 billion Alabama snapshot, and $1.5 billion 2026-2027 expansion plan; none is summed or allocated to the selected building. The 2018 location-page opening milestone conflicts with the 2026 release's 2019 operations start, so both are preserved as a chronology conflict.

source.title: Jackson County, Alabama — Google Data Center Location
source.notes: Current location page reports more than $2 billion of Alabama data-center investment since 2018, more than $28 million of statewide philanthropic giving since 2009, more than 153,000 Alabamians trained through over 100 organizations, 17,000 small businesses trained, and 2025 statewide digital economic activity of $2.6 billion. Only investment and giving map to governed direct metrics; the broader digital-activity figure is not a facility contribution estimate.

research_updates.title: Assessor and tax-payment evidence matrix
research_updates.notes: Queried owner Google and exact address 48809 AL Hwy 277 in the Jackson County Revenue Commissioner portal. Retained every 2020-2025 appraised value, assessed value and paid tax for accounts 151335/PPIN 50326 (Google), 151342/PPIN 50327 (Design), and 151344/PPIN 50328 (Wiessner); Google is named in payment memos on the two non-Google accounts in 2021-2024, and Design's Google subsidiary status is independently documented. Excluded the three accounts' unpaid 2026 estimates and exact-address ADP and Schenker results because no project relationship was established. No real-property parcel, recipient distribution, abated-tax counterfactual, complete affiliate roster or audit of campus-account completeness was found.

source.title: Jackson County property and tax history — Google LLC account 151335
source.notes: Official live account at 48809 AL Hwy 277, PPIN 50326, personal-property district COUNTY-SCHOOL DISTRICT 1, exemption codes AB and PP. Tax-history rows provide exact appraised, assessed and paid amounts for 2020-2025; the unpaid 2026 estimate is excluded.

research_updates.title: Incentive, public-cost and debt gap closure
research_updates.notes: Searched Alabama Revenue Chapter 9B guidance, Alabama Commerce/ADECA records, Alabama Examiners audit search and Jackson County Commission agendas/minutes for 2018-2026. Program rules confirm possible 10-, 20- or 30-year data-center abatements and require an executed agreement, but no Google/Design/Wiessner agreement, amendment, compliance report, certified $50 million investment-credit value, $20 million sales-tax abatement, $11.8 million property-tax abatement, or $109 million ten-year state impact figure was found in a primary project record; those secondary-source figures are rejected. No project-specific public infrastructure cost, operating subsidy, debt, bond, reimbursement, clawback, tax-recipient allocation or same-scope marginal service cost was located; net fiscal modeling is ineligible, while exact annual tax aggregation and an equal-cost threshold are eligible.

source.title: Chapter 9B Abatements
source.notes: Official program rules allow qualifying data-processing-center property and sales/use abatements for 10, 20 or 30 years depending on documented investment thresholds and require an executed agreement specifying estimated taxes, term, investment and employment/payroll projections. No Google-specific executed agreement, amendment, compliance schedule or abated-tax amount was located.

research_updates.title: Planning, permit, contractor and supplier search
research_updates.notes: Reviewed OSHA Partnership 907, TVA Widows Creek disposition records, Jackson County indexed agendas/minutes, operator releases and local planning/permit search results. OSHA supplies 465 +/- acres, multiple two-story facilities, 60 MW per facility, Holder construction management and major MEP/steel/precast/site-work categories; TVA separately reports 566 acres sold. No building count, permit number/value, certificate of occupancy, selected-building square footage, construction contract value, supplier invoice, local vendor roster/payment, residence share, wage ledger or procurement spend was found. Catalog-and-record proposals: study.planned_data_center_power_capacity (MW, construction/source projection, one 60 MW per described facility), study.project_site_area (acres, investment/reported actual, 465 +/- OSHA project boundary and separate 566-acre TVA sale); schema needs an acres unit before publication.

source.title: OSHA Strategic Partnership #907 — Widows Creek Project
source.publisher: U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration
source.notes: Federal construction partnership describes a 465 +/- acre Bridgeport greenfield project with multiple two-story 60 MW data-center facilities and support buildings, structural steel and precast skin, exterior electrical and mechanical cooling plant, Holder Construction Group construction management and self-performed concrete, plus MEP, steel, precast and site-work trades.

research_updates.title: Utility, load, generation and resource search
research_updates.notes: Reviewed Google releases/location materials, TVA annual and Widows Creek records, ADEM eFile/EPA facility search, and available Bridgeport/Jackson County water records. Retained 2024 withdrawal of approximately 201.6 million gallons; modeled rows preserve reported 2022-2024 consumption/discharge/PUE/CFE values without allocating a building. More than 300 MW contracted regional generation and up to 50 MW shared Tennessee/Alabama advanced nuclear supply are not campus load or facility capacity; catalog proposal study.contracted_regional_generation_capacity (MW, resources/source projection) would retain them only at utility-service-area and multi-state scope. No facility electricity meter/load, tariff payment, interconnection cost, water entitlement/rate/payment, discharge permit/limit, backup-generator count, project air emissions, violation, renewable-energy payment or selected-building resource allocation was found.

source.title: Google Strengthens Alabama Presence With New Data Center Investment, Community Initiatives
source.notes: Three-page release reports the $1.5 billion 2026-2027 expansion, $2 million Energy Impact Fund, $550,000 school donation, more than 1,000 construction contract workers, more than 300 MW contracted regional generation, up to 50 MW advanced nuclear supply shared by Tennessee and Alabama data centers, three stabilized erosion sites, more than 1,500 robotics participants, more than 6,000 statewide volunteer hours, and broader statewide training statistics. The release says operations began in 2019, conflicting with the current location page's 2018 opening milestone.

research_updates.title: Workforce, operations and compensation evidence matrix
research_updates.notes: Retained separately the up-to-100-job 2018 plan, TVA's nearly-70-job FY2020 result, the 2023 approximately 230 direct-and-indirect job snapshot with an approximately 100-Google-employee component, the greater-than-1,800 historical construction workforce, and the greater-than-1,000-worker 2026 expansion statement. None is converted to FTE, job-years, payroll, wages, benefits, residence or current headcount. Google careers, OSHA, operator releases, state workforce materials and county sources supplied no roster, occupation mix, facility payroll, contractor payroll, hours, union status, turnover or vendor employment ledger, so compensation and further workforce modeling are rejected.

source.title: Google makes an impact in Jackson County
source.notes: Contemporaneous local reporting attributes workforce and community figures to Jackson County Economic Development Authority and school officials: about 230 direct and indirect jobs, about 100 Google employees, more than 1,800 construction workers, a $50,000 school-year grant, $100,000 for county library programs and more than $750,000 in grants. These named-source figures are not audited payroll or recipient ledgers.

research_updates.title: Source-modeled economic contribution disposition
research_updates.notes: The Deloitte/Google study's annual-average 2021-2023 Alabama outputs are retained only as visibly source-modeled estimates: about $77 million GDP ($42 million direct, $19 million indirect, $16 million induced), about 690 jobs (255/270/165), and about $47 million labor income ($19 million/$20 million/$8 million). Its approximately $520,000 carbon-free-energy GDP and $230,000 labor-income outputs, 42% professional/technical GDP share, 58% other-sector share, 21% modeled GDP growth versus 8% Alabama GDP growth, $2.40 social benefit per dollar, and 2022-2023 environmental percentages receive explicit model disposition rather than direct-actual treatment. The approximately 790 household equivalents are not retained with a jobs surrogate: catalog proposal study.household_income_equivalents needs a households unit and a source-modeled record. The reported 83% PUE-overhead reduction versus 1.58 industry PUE is not a facility contribution or electricity saving; catalog proposal study.pue_overhead_reduction_vs_industry needs percent, benchmark vintage and formula fields before direct/context publication. No building-level allocation, observed payroll, observed supplier spending or causal effect is inferred.

source.title: Google's Data Center Impact in Alabama — 2024 Impact Study
source.publisher: Google LLC and Deloitte Consulting LLP
source.notes: Six-page Deloitte study prepared for Google from Google, public, and third-party inputs without independent verification. Source-modeled outputs remain modeled, not observed.

research_updates.title: Community recipient and beneficiary reconciliation
research_updates.notes: Cross-checked operator totals against Mountain Lakes Chamber and NACC recipient records. Retained monetary contributions at their native recipient/period scopes and marked overlap: $50,000 school grant, $100,000 library aggregate, greater than $750,000 local grants, approximately $1.1 million to 22 organizations, greater than $100,000 for NACC, $57,000 for YouScience, and the $2 million/$550,000 2026 announcements. Catalog-and-record proposals are required for nonmonetary outputs: study.community_organizations_supported (organizations: 22), study.community_program_participants (participants/students: about 100 NACC, over 7,500 YouScience in the Google study, 2,221 participation and 1,327 completions in the recipient report, over 60 NACC campers, over 1,500 robotics participants), study.volunteer_hours (hours: over 6,000 statewide), and study.recipient_program_expenditure (USD: $359.24 NACC Google STEM Camp fund expense). No transaction-complete disbursement or overlap ledger was found.

source.title: 2024 Annual Mountain Lakes Chamber Report
source.notes: Recipient report confirms a three-year $57,000 Google grant for YouScience and reports 2,221 participating students and 1,327 completed aptitude/career-discovery exercises in its 2024 program description. Wider work-based-learning wages and hours have multiple partners and are not attributed to Google.

research_updates.title: County GDP, employment and wage design disposition
research_updates.notes: The official-source repository panel has complete positive Jackson County GDP, covered-employment and nominal weekly-wage observations for 2010-2017 and 2024. Three reproducible inverse-distance 20-county comparisons are retained as low-confidence descriptive gaps with fit-sensitivity envelopes, not causal effects; the 2018/2019 chronology conflict, construction, later expansions and concurrent county changes defeat causal identification. No facility wage series, isolated treatment timing, verified uncontaminated donor pool, placebos, spillover rule or causal robustness package was found.

source.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis and U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
source.notes: Repository panel compiled from official annual county real GDP, covered employment and nominal average-weekly-wage series. The model uses Jackson County's 2010-2017 pre-period and 2024 outcome; source revisions and concurrent treatments remain limitations.

research_updates.title: Adversarial state-project and compensation follow-up
research_updates.notes: The directed corrective search found Alabama Commerce’s Project Spike profile after the candidate commit. The 350-acre state planning boundary is preserved alongside, not substituted for, OSHA’s 465 +/- acre construction boundary and TVA’s 566-acre sale; the 75-100 employee range remains a projection because the article conflicts with the later 2019 operating chronology. Catalog-and-record proposals: study.direct_payroll_projection (USD, operations/source projection, greater than $93.6 million over a 20-year horizon) and study.projected_economic_impact (USD, operations/source projection, $129 million over 20 years with definition required). Only the payroll floor is eligible for a deterministic annualized model; the undefined economic-impact aggregate is rejected from synthesis.

source.title: How Google’s Search Ended in Alabama
source.notes: State project profile identifies the recruitment codename Project Spike and reports a 350-acre planning boundary, a 75-100 employee full-operation range, a projected $129 million economic impact over 20 years, and projected direct wages greater than $93.6 million over 20 years. Its 2016 language alternates between completed and future operation even though later operator and local-utility records put operations in 2019, so the prospective figures are not treated as realized facts.

research_updates.title: Adversarial utility and chronology cross-check
research_updates.notes: North Alabama Electric Cooperative independently corroborates a 2019 operating start and clarifies that more than 1,000 contract workers are expected through 2027, supporting the existing two-year projection horizon. Its nearly-60% TVA carbon-free system share is not substituted for the Google impact study’s 52%/53% regional-grid vintages or 63%/65% site match and does not identify NAEC as the retail supplier to the campus. Repeated EPA/ECHO, ADEM, NAEC, TVA and FERC searches still found no project facility identifier, meter, tariff, bill, load, interconnection filing or priced infrastructure obligation.

source.title: Generational change — Google commits $1.5 billion for data center expansion, area programs
source.notes: Local cooperative publication corroborates 2019 operations, the $1.5 billion expansion, $550,000 school donation, $2 million fund and more-than-1,000 contract-worker plan; it says expansion completion is expected in 2027. Its nearly-60% TVA carbon-free share is a utility-system statement, not campus supply or a Google meter.

research_updates.title: Adversarial source-family negatives queued for corrective audit
research_updates.notes: Contract 3.1.0 adversarial correction completed after candidate commit e3a0b32ae0954ed38c9875674d3c1238144b6a6a. Rechecks found no Google-specific EPA/ADEM facility match, permit, executed incentive, facility load, priced utility obligation, supplier payment or payroll ledger; they did find the Alabama Commerce and NAEC sources recorded separately. Corrective changes remove the invalid jobs-unit household-equivalent model, remove helper-only schema fields, repair the three-account break-even parameter provenance, annualize only the explicit 20-year wage projection floor, and add explicit dispositions for the 83% overhead-reduction and approximately 790-household claims.

source.title: ADEM eFile public document search
source.notes: Facility/county searches covering Google, Design LLC, 48809 AL Hwy 277, Bridgeport, Jackson County and Widows Creek did not yield a project-specific air, water or waste permit with generator count, emissions, discharge limit, water entitlement, compliance expenditure or violation penalty. TVA legacy coal/CCR records were not treated as Google operating records.

research_updates.title: Orchestrator adopted direct environmental, boundary and payroll records
research_updates.notes: The orchestrator moved 12 source-reported PUE, hourly carbon-free-energy, water-consumption and discharge values out of modeled synthesis and into governed direct records, then added separate 350-, approximately 465-, and 566-acre boundaries, the per-facility 60 MW design projection, and the greater-than-$93.6 million direct-payroll projection. The 12 duplicate environmental models were retired. Thirty residual models remain for source-modeled economics, the lower-bound payroll annualization, exact tax aggregation, an equal-cost threshold and descriptive county comparisons.
